findings.title: branch_checkout never deserializes: UI sends opts:{} but Rust CheckoutOptions.detach is a required field
findings.evidence: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/domain/refs.rs:41-45 — `#[derive(...)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct CheckoutOptions { pub detach: bool }` has NO #[serde(default)] on the struct or the field, so `detach` is a required key. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/bridges/commands.ts:152-158 defaults `opts: CheckoutOptions = {}` and always sends `args: { repo, name, opts }`. The only call site, /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/branches.ts:63, is `commands.branchCheckout(repo, name, {})`. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/commands/branches.rs:104-105 has `#[serde(default)]` on `opts` only (that default applies when `opts` is absent, not when it is `{}`). /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/bridges/bindings.ts:233-235 declares `detach?: boolean` (optional), so the TS side believes it may omit it. CLAUDE.md:68-69 states the invariant this breaks: 'every field the frontend can omit carries #[serde(default)]'.
findings.repro: Open any repository, go to the Branches tab, double-click a local branch row (or click the sidebar row's ⋯, or the palette's branch item, or the detail pane's Checkout button). Same for the toolbar Branch ▾ → Checkout branch. Any of these calls App.vue:875 `branches.checkout(branch?.name ?? name)` → stores/branches.ts:63 `branchCheckout(repo, name, {})`.
findings.expected: HEAD switches to the branch, a success toast '已签出分支 X' appears, and the working copy/branch list reload.
findings.actual: Tauri fails while deserializing the command arguments (missing field `detach`), before AppState::run is ever entered, so the engine never runs and HEAD never moves. The rejection is not an ErrorPayload, so App.vue:548-554 reportError() cannot read `.message` and falls back to the generic toast '无法签出该分支。' ('Could not check out the branch.') with no cause — exactly the owner's 'fails with no error shown'. Checkout is unreachable from every entry point in the branch surface.
findings.fix: Add `#[serde(default)]` to CheckoutOptions (container level) in src-tauri/src/domain/refs.rs, matching the crate convention used by MergeOptions/RebaseOptions (commands/integrate.rs:78-79, 226-227). Optionally also change the bridge default to an explicit `{ detach: false }` so the payload is self-describing. Independently, make reportError() fall back to `errorText()` (see BR-07) so a non-ErrorPayload rejection still tells the user something.
findings.testIdea: src-tauri: a unit test in src-tauri/src/domain/refs.rs (or tests/) asserting `serde_json::from_value::<CheckoutOptions>(serde_json::json!({}))` is `Ok` and yields `detach == false`. Frontend: src/stores/branches.test.ts — invoke the store's `checkout('r', 'main')` against a mocked `commands.branchCheckout` and assert it was called with a full options object (`expect(branchCheckout).toHaveBeenCalledWith('r', 'main', { detach: false })`), which fails today with `{}` only if the mock is typed as the Rust shape.

findings.title: Toolbar Fetch always fails: `remote_fetch` is sent a string where Rust expects a struct
findings.evidence: src/bridges/commands.ts:291-298 — `remoteFetch(repo, remote, refspecs = [], mode = "default")` always includes `mode` in the payload: `invoke("remote_fetch", { args: { repo, remote, refspecs, mode } })`. src/bridges/bindings.ts:485 declares `RemoteFetchMode = "default" | "prune" | "tags" | "pruneTags"`. Rust's field is a struct: src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:40 imports `RemoteFetchMode` from `crate::engine::remotes`, and src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:56-65 defines it as `struct RemoteFetchMode { prune: bool, tags: TagFetch, depth: Option<i32> }` with `#[serde(default, rename_all = "camelCase")]`. src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:687-694 is the args struct (`#[serde(default)] pub mode: RemoteFetchMode`) — `default` only applies when the key is ABSENT, and the frontend always sends it. Only caller: src/composables/useGit.ts:56-61. docs/03-command-surface.md:241 documents the wire shape as `opts{prune, tags, ...}`, confirming the intent.
findings.repro: Open any repository that has a remote and press 工具栏 → 抓取. The invoke payload is `{args:{repo,remote,refspecs:[],mode:"default"}}`. serde fails to deserialize the string into the struct, so the command rejects before `RemoteFetch::validate` (refs.rs:696-706) ever runs.
findings.expected: `git fetch <remote>` runs, the remote-tracking refs update, FetchReport is returned and the branch list's ahead/behind badges refresh.
findings.actual: The promise rejects with a serde string ("invalid type: string \"default\", expected struct RemoteFetchMode"). useGit.run (useGit.ts:45-47) stores that raw string in `lastError`; runVerb (App.vue:580-584) shows only the generic "操作失败。" toast and records `error.message === undefined` in the activity list. Fetch has never worked in this build, and the failure reads like a network problem rather than a broken call.
findings.fix: Stop sending the key from the wrapper — omit `mode`/`refspecs` unless the caller supplies them so the Rust `#[serde(default)]` applies — and type the parameter as the Rust struct (`{prune?: boolean; tags?: TagFetch; depth?: number}`). Better: rename the engine struct (e.g. `RemoteFetchOptions`) so it stops colliding with `domain::repository::RemoteFetchMode`, which is a different two-value enum (domain/repository.rs:187-196). Also wire or refuse `remote_prune` — with the current defaults `prune:false` and no caller passing it, stale tracking refs can never be pruned from the UI.
findings.testIdea: Add `#[cfg(test)] mod wire` to src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs: `serde_json::from_value::<RemoteFetch>(json!({"repo":"x","remote":"origin","refspecs":[],"mode":"default"}))` must be Ok, and `json!({"repo":"x","remote":"origin"})` must also be Ok. On the frontend, add src/bridges/commands.test.ts that mocks `@tauri-apps/api/core`'s `invoke` and asserts `remoteFetch("r","origin")` sends no `mode` key (and `remotePull`/`remotePublishBranch` send the keys the Rust structs actually declare).

findings.title: Checking out a remote-tracking branch whose short name already exists locally always fails
findings.evidence: /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/stores/branches.ts:72-86: `checkoutRemote` computes `suggestedName` = the short name ('main' from 'origin/main') and then deliberately passes `localName = nameExists ? undefined : suggestedName`. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src-tauri/src/engine/branches.rs:584 raises ReferenceExists when the local name is taken: `let name = local_name.unwrap_or(&short); if repo.find_branch(&name, Local).is_ok() { return Err(... "Branch '{name}' already exists") }` — and the same check is duplicated at 586-600. So when the local branch exists the UI withholds the name and the engine then re-derives exactly that name and refuses. Reached from /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/App.vue:855-869 (checkoutFlow's `branch?.isRemote === true` arm), i.e. row dblclick (App.vue:1592), the checkout dialogue (App.vue:842-849 lists allBranches with emitFullName), and the palette only lists locals so it is unaffected.
findings.repro: In a normal clone (local `main` tracking `origin/main`), open the Branches tab, set the filter to 全部 or 远程, and double-click the `origin/main` row. Verified against real git in /tmp/audit-branch: with `main` and `origin/main` present, `git checkout main` switches to the local branch and reports '您的分支与上游分支 origin/main 一致'.
findings.expected: Switch to the existing local branch `main` (what `git checkout main` does), or, if the user really wants a second branch at origin/main's tip, ask for a distinct name.
findings.actual: English toast 'Branch \'main\' already exists' in the zh-CN UI and no checkout. The obvious intent — get onto main — is refused with no way forward, because nothing in the branch surface exposes a name prompt for this verb.
findings.fix: In stores/branches.ts:72-86, when `nameExists` is true, check out the existing local branch instead of calling checkout_remote (i.e. fall through to `commands.branchCheckout(repo, suggestedName)`), or pass a de-duplicated name such as `main-2` and surface it in the toast. Fix the engine's duplicated existence check at engine/branches.rs:586-600 at the same time.
findings.testIdea: src/stores/branches.test.ts — with a store fixture where `branches = [{name:'main'}]` and a mocked `branchCheckoutRemote`, call `checkoutRemote('refs/remotes/origin/main')` and assert the local branch path is taken (`expect(branchCheckout).toHaveBeenCalledWith(repo,'main',...)`) rather than `branchCheckoutRemote` with `localName === undefined`.

findings.title: Toolbar Push pushes the branch that was checked out when the repo was opened, not the current HEAD
findings.evidence: src/composables/useGit.ts:75-84 — `const branch = branchName ?? repos.selected?.headBranch`. src/App.vue:671-672 calls `git.push()` with no argument. `repos.selected` is `repositories.value.find(...)` (src/stores/repos.ts:27-29) and the only writer of `repositories` is `upsert` (repos.ts:36-43), called from open/init/clone only (repos.ts:61, 78, 124). Nothing refreshes RepoInfo afterwards: useAppEvents.ts:26-29 makes `reposChanged` a no-op, and there is no `repositoryRefresh` wrapper in src/bridges/commands.ts although the Rust command is registered at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:69. `headBranch` is read as "the current branch" in four other places (App.vue:207, 225-226, 596, 847, 1608), so the staleness is visible beyond push.
findings.repro: Open repo A whose HEAD is `main` (RepoInfo.headBranch = "main"), check out `feature` (App.vue:875 → branches.checkout → `branch_checkout`), then press 工具栏 → 推送.
findings.expected: `feature` is published — the toolbar's own disabled reason (App.vue:609, zh-CN "HEAD 处于游离状态 —— 请先签出分支再推送。") promises the verb means "push HEAD".
findings.actual: `repos.selected.headBranch` is still "main", so `remotePublishBranch(id, "origin", "main")` re-pushes main. Because origin already has main, the push is a no-op fast-forward that succeeds, and the toast claims 已推送. `feature` is never published; its row still shows ahead>0 with no upstream, and the window subtitle still says "在 main 上".
findings.fix: Resolve the branch from the live branch list (`branches.branches.value.find(b => b.isHead)?.name`) or pass the branch down from the list, and add a `repositoryRefresh` bridge so RepoInfo.headBranch is re-read on refsChanged (which also fixes the stale subtitle and the "Merge into <old branch>" label).

findings.title: Commit composer survives a repository switch, so the next commit amends the wrong repository's HEAD
findings.evidence: src/App.vue:935-938 declares composerSubject/composerBody/composerAmend/composerSignOff; the only place they are cleared is App.vue:1005-1007 inside commitNow() after a successful commit. The existing repository watch App.vue:520-524 (`watch(activeRepoId, (id) => compare.forRepo(id ?? null))`) resets compare but nothing resets the composer. commitNow() (App.vue:987-1014) sends whatever is in those refs to workingCopy.commit -> commitAmend/commitCreate (src/stores/workingCopy.ts:68-84) with repo = repos.selectedId, i.e. the NEW repository. The switcher is always enabled (App.vue:1417 `:locked="false"`), so the switch is reachable mid-edit.
findings.repro: Open repository A, type subject "fix parser" in the working-copy composer, tick Amend (can-amend is true because A has a HEAD). Without committing, use the sidebar RepoSwitcher to switch to repository B. Stage any file in B and press Commit. Expected: B's commit uses B's own composer (empty subject, Amend off). Actual: `commit_amend` is invoked against B with message "fix parser", rewriting B's HEAD commit.
findings.expected: Switching the selected repository resets the composer (subject, body, amend, sign-off) — no input meant for repository A can be submitted against repository B.
findings.actual: composerSubject/composerBody/composerAmend/composerSignOff are shell-level refs that outlive the repository selection, so A's message and A's amend tick are applied to B, silently rewriting an unrelated repository's HEAD commit.
findings.fix: In the existing `watch(activeRepoId, ...)` at App.vue:520-524, clear composerSubject.value = "", composerBody.value = "", composerAmend.value = false, composerSignOff.value = false (and selectedPath.value = null, conflictedOnly.value = false) whenever the id actually changes.

findings.evidence: src/bridges/commands.ts:191-197 sends `{args:{repo, paths, opts}}` with opts defaulted to `{}`; src/stores/workingCopy.ts:52-61 calls it with no options; the only caller is App.vue:918. src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs:269-273 hits `if status.contains(Status::WT_NEW) && !tracked { if opts.include_untracked { to_delete.push(..) } continue; }` — with include_untracked=false the path is skipped and the function returns Ok(()) having written nothing; src-tauri/src/domain/working_copy.rs:519-529 declares `include_untracked: false` by default, and src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:412-415 returns `changed(cx)` (a fresh delta still containing the file). App.vue:919 then pushes the success toast for `ok === true`.

Working copy tab → the file appears in the 未跟踪 section; hover the row and click the ↩ discard button (WorkingCopyFileList.vue:159-167; the detail bar's 放弃 button is shown for every non-staged, non-unmerged entry, WorkingCopyFileDetail.vue:105-113). 3. findings.title: HEAD is never re-read after a checkout, so the toolbar's Push and Commit & Push publish the wrong branch
findings.evidence: RepoInfo (headBranch/headOid/state) is only written by repos.upsert, which is called solely from open/init/clone (src/stores/repos.ts:36-43, 61, 78, 124). branches.checkout (src/stores/branches.ts:60-70) runs branch_checkout then refresh() of the branch list only — it never updates RepoInfo, and useGit.refreshAll (src/composables/useGit.ts:32-34) refreshes branches/working-copy/history only. The engine command that would fix this, `repository_refresh` (src-tauri/src/commands/repository.rs:259-302, registered at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:69), has NO bridge in src/bridges/commands.ts and no entry in src/bridges/bindings.ts, so nothing in the UI can call it. Consumers of the stale value: windowSubtitle (App.vue:220-227, renders "On {branch}"), RepoSwitcher head label (src/layout/RepoSwitcher.vue:85), toolbar pushReason/detachedHead (App.vue:604-610), can-amend (App.vue:1483). git.push() with no name reads repos.selected?.headBranch (src/composables/useGit.ts:75-84) and the engine pushes that named ref: engine/remotes.rs:982 builds refspec `refs/heads/{branch}:refs/heads/{branch}`.
findings.repro: In repository R on branch main, use the branch pane to check out feature (or `git switch -c feature` in a terminal). Press Push on the toolbar (or Commit & Push on the commit split button, App.vue:1022). Expected: `feature` is published. Actual: headBranch is still "main", so remote_publish_branch is called with branch="main" and refs/heads/main is pushed; feature's commits never reach the remote and the success toast fires anyway. Established with the git CLI in /tmp/audit-shell/gitlab: with HEAD on `feature`, `git push origin main:main` leaves origin at refs/heads/main=3f2a300 (the pre-feature commit) and pushes nothing of feature.
findings.expected: After a checkout (in-app or external) the shell's repository model reflects the new HEAD, so the window subtitle, the switcher and every push path name the branch that is actually checked out.
findings.actual: headBranch/headOid/state are frozen at open time; after a checkout the subtitle still reads "On main", and the toolbar Push / Commit & Push publish `main` while the user is on `feature` — a silent wrong-ref push to a remote, reported as success.
findings.fix: Add a `repositoryRefresh(repo)` bridge for the already-registered `repository_refresh` and call it (or re-read RepoInfo via it) after every command that can move HEAD: branch checkout/create/rename/delete, commit/amend, merge/rebase/continue/abort, fetch/pull/push, discard. Alternatively have useGit.run refresh the RepoInfo of the repo it acted on and upsert it.

findings.title: `remotePublishBranch` is always called with `setUpstream:false`, overriding the Rust default, so a first push can never record tracking
findings.evidence: src/bridges/commands.ts:309-319 — `setUpstream = false` and the key is always included. src/composables/useGit.ts:83 calls it with three arguments. Rust declares the opposite default: src-tauri/src/commands/refs.rs:888-895 `#[serde(default = "default_true")] pub set_upstream: bool` (default_true at refs.rs:1712). src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:1006-1012 writes `branch.<name>.remote`/`.merge` only when `set_upstream` is true, while src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:1014-1018 documents `PublishReport.upstream` as "the upstream shorthand that was recorded" and reports it unconditionally.
findings.repro: Create branch `feature`, then press 推送 in the branch pane (App.vue:1613 → pushSelectedBranch → `git.push("feature")`). Verified with the git CLI in /tmp/audit-remotes: `git push origin feature` writes no `branch.feature.*`; `git push -u origin feature` writes `branch.feature.remote=origin` and `branch.feature.merge=refs/heads/feature`.
findings.expected: `git push -u` semantics (the engine's own doc comment at engine/remotes.rs:976-977 calls this command "push a local branch and make it the upstream"): tracking is recorded, so the row shows `origin/feature` and ahead/behind.

The composer gate `props.subject.trim() !== "" && stagedCount.value > 0` (src/components/panes/CommitComposer.vue:64-73) and App.vue:989 refuse it before the command is even issued, and the merge banner that carries the 「提交合并」 button (WorkingCopyPane.vue:200-226) is fed by `const mergeStatus = ref<MergeStatus | null>(null)` (src/App.vue:1031) — never assigned, so `wc_merge_status_load` (src/bridges/commands.ts:355-357) is dead code.
findings.repro: 1. Create a conflicting merge. 2. Resolve the conflict by taking ours (`git checkout --ours .` + stage, or the app's resolve flow) so the index tree equals HEAD's tree. 3. Verified with git 2.45: `git commit -m 'merge resolved as ours'` succeeds and writes a two-parent merge commit. 4. In Meridian the Commit button is disabled with 「先暂存改动」 and the merge banner is absent, so the only remaining exit (`resolveMerge`/`abortMerge` at App.vue:1509-1510) is also invisible — the merge cannot be completed from the UI.
findings.expected: While a merge is in progress, `git commit`'s rule applies: the commit is allowed even when the index matches HEAD (that is how a merge resolved entirely to 'ours' is finished), producing the two-parent merge commit.
findings.actual: Commit is refused with 「No staged changes to commit」 (invalid_request) because the index tree equals HEAD's tree, and the Commit button is disabled with 「先暂存改动」 — so the merge cannot be completed at all.
findings.fix: In `validate_commit`, skip the `!staged` refusal when `repo.state() == RepositoryState::Merge`; mirror that in the composer (App.vue:989 / CommitComposer.vue:64-73) by passing a `mergeInProgress` prop so the staged-count gate does not apply. Separately, wire `wcMergeStatusLoad` into the store so the banner (and its 提交合并 button) actually renders.
findings.testIdea: src-tauri/src/commands/commit.rs tests: build a conflicted merge (the `conflicting_merge` helper in src-tauri/src/engine/index.rs:1534), resolve it to HEAD's content, then assert `validate_commit` returns Ok and `commit()` yields `parent_count == 2`.

findings.title: Bulk stage/unstage issues one command per path, each re-reading the whole status, with no progress and no error
findings.evidence: src/components/panes/WorkingCopyPane.vue:155-159 collects the section's paths and emits them; src/App.vue:1497-1498 turns that into `paths.forEach(path => void workingCopy.stage(path))`; src/stores/workingCopy.ts:35-49 issues one `wc_stage_paths` per path; src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:668-677 (`changed`) re-runs a full `engine::status::load` and ships the entire delta back for **every** one of them. `wc_stage_all` / `wc_unstage_all` (src-tauri/src/commands/working_copy.rs:213-284, registered at lib.rs:82-83) exist and would do it in one call, but no TS wrapper exists.
findings.repro: 1. Check out a repository with a large untracked/generated tree (20k files). 2. Working copy → 未跟踪 section → 暂存所有. 3. The app issues 20,000 `wc_stage_paths` commands; each one walks the whole worktree for status and returns the full delta over IPC. The list freezes with no busy indicator, and if any single call fails the error state is overwritten by the next success (see WC-12) so the user is told nothing.
findings.expected: One command for the whole section (paths array or `wc_stage_all`), with a busy indicator and one reported error.
findings.actual: The section's 「暂存所有」/「取消暂存所有」 buttons fire one IPC command per file, and every command re-scans the entire working copy and returns the full delta — O(N) full status walks, no progress, and the UI becomes unresponsive on any real tree.
findings.fix: Add `wcStageAll`/`wcUnstageAll` wrappers in src/bridges/commands.ts and call them for the section bulk buttons (or send the whole `paths` array in one `wc_stage_paths`); wrap the call in a `busy` flag and report a single error toast.
findings.testIdea: src/App.test.ts (or a mounted WorkingCopyPane test): with 5 rows in a section, clicking the bulk button must produce exactly one invoke of `wc_stage_paths` with the 5-path array (or one `wc_stage_all`), not 5 invokes.

findings.title: No generation guard on history refresh: the list and the graph can show a different query than the search box
findings.evidence: src/App.vue:1075-1078 fires `void history.setQuery(historyQuery())` on every keystroke (no debounce, result not awaited); src/composables/useHistory.ts:36-39 -> src/stores/history.ts:85-95: `refresh` sets loading, then `apply(await commands.historyCommitsLoad(...))` and `await loadGraph(repo)` with no token; `apply` (stores/history.ts:54-59) overwrites commits/truncated/state unconditionally, and `loadGraph` (71-83) writes graph.value unconditionally. The layout is consumed positionally, so a layout from query A rendered against commits from query B is silently wrong, not missing: src/components/commit-list/VirtualCommitList.vue:174-188 (`layout.lanes[commitIndex]`) and 253-258 (`segmentIdsAt(index, commitIndex)`). src/composables/useCompare.ts:120-146 shows the token pattern the history store lacks.
findings.repro: Open a repo with a few thousand commits. Put the caret in 搜索提交 and type `fix` quickly. Each keystroke issues history_commits_load + history_graph_compute; a 1-character query walks far more commits than a 3-character one, so the earlier response often lands last. The box reads `fix` while the list holds the matches for `f`, and if the graph response interleaves, `layout` is the lane array for `f` while `commits` is `fi`, so every row is painted with another commit's lane and stroke set.
findings.expected: The rows, the graph and the selection always correspond to the current search text / sort / first-parent; a superseded or out-of-order response is discarded.
findings.actual: Last response to arrive wins. commits and graph are applied independently, so the two can come from different queries and the screen shows the wrong rows and a mis-paired graph with no indication.

Debounce the App.vue watcher (~150-200ms) or await the previous refresh. Also drop the second round trip per keystroke: HistoryPage already carries `graph` (src-tauri/src/domain/commit.rs:290-292, computed in engine/history.rs:207-214), so `refresh` can use `toGraphLayout(page.graph)` instead of calling history_graph_compute again.

findings.title: Repository can be switched mid-operation (locked hard-coded false, useGit.busy unread) and the in-flight result is applied to the new repository
findings.evidence: App.vue:1417 passes `:locked="false"` to AppSidebar, whose RepoSwitcher documents the prop as "Disables the switcher while a blocking operation runs" (src/layout/RepoSwitcher.vue:19-22, 72, 77). useGit exposes `busy` (src/composables/useGit.ts:26) and it is read nowhere in the app (grep finds only its declaration). useGit.run captures the id but then calls refreshAll(id) (useGit.ts:36-51), and each store refresh writes shared state with no check that the repo it was issued for is still selected: src/stores/branches.ts:24-39, src/stores/workingCopy.ts:26-33, src/stores/history.ts:85-95. The event path does guard — useAppEvents.ts:31-39 returns unless `event.payload.repo === repos.selectedId` — so the two paths disagree about the hazard.
findings.repro: Open repositories A and B. Select A and press Fetch against a slow/large remote (or clone a large repository and switch away while it runs). Switch to B via the RepoSwitcher. B's lists load. When A's request resolves, refreshAll(A) overwrites branches/working-copy/history with A's data while the route, window title and switcher all say B. Selecting a file in that stale working-copy list then calls wc_stage_paths(B, [A's path]).
findings.expected: A response for repository A must never be written into state that is displaying repository B; the switcher should be disabled (with a reason) while a blocking operation runs.
findings.actual: The response is applied unconditionally, so the sidebar, working-copy list and history show the previous repository's contents under the new repository's title, and a subsequent action derived from that list targets the wrong repository.
findings.fix: Guard every store write with the repo it was issued for (drop the response when `repo !== repos.selectedId`), and pass `:locked="git.busy || repositories.busy || activity.running.length > 0"` to AppSidebar so the switcher stops claiming it is fine to switch.

findings.title: A status/delta response for another repository is applied to the current one (cross-repo race)

The watcher at src/composables/useWorkingCopy.ts:16-22 issues `store.refresh(id)` on every selection change, and `store.commit` (workingCopy.ts:68-84) refreshes the id it captured at call time. `repositories.select(id)` (src/stores/repos.ts:36-38 via src/composables/useRepositories.ts:72-74, reached from the command palette / recents list at App.vue:526-529 and 1332) does not clear the working-copy store.
findings.repro: 1. Open a repository with a large working copy (a slow `wc_status_load`). 2. Before it answers, switch to another repository (command palette → Open, or the recents list). 3. findings.title: branch_delete's DeleteReport is discarded, so a skipped deletion is reported as a successful one
findings.evidence: engine/branches.rs:344-389 returns `DeleteReport { deleted, skipped }` and never errors on a skip: a branch that no longer exists lands in `skipped` with class 'reference_not_found' (357-364), the checked-out branch with 'branch_is_head' (366-373), an unmerged one with 'delete_unmerged_branch' (375-382). The type's own doc (engine/branches.rs:27-29) says branches that vanished between the UI's snapshot and the command 'land in skipped … instead of failing the whole batch'. findings.evidence: src/bridges/bindings.ts:485 declares `RemoteFetchMode` as the 4-value string union used by F1, while the Rust side has two same-named types: src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:56-65 (the options struct) and src-tauri/src/domain/repository.rs:187-196 (a two-value `All|Specified` enum, which is what `repository_remotes_load` actually serialises — as "all"/"specified"). src/bridges/bindings.ts:487-490 declares `PullOptions.mode` as `"merge"|"rebase"|"ffOnly"` while src-tauri/src/engine/remotes.rs:136-147 renames `FastForwardOnly` to `"fastForwardOnly"`, so `"ffOnly"` is not a valid variant. src/bridges/bindings.ts:492-500 declares `fetchUrl`/`pushUrl`, while src-tauri/src/domain/repository.rs:198-208 with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` serialises `url`/`pushurl` — `RepositoryRemote.fetchUrl` is therefore `undefined` at runtime.

findings.title: There is no way to choose, add or inspect a remote, and `defaultRemote` picks one by array order

The same column binds `@contextmenu.prevent="emit('contextmenu', …)"` (WorkingCopyFileList.vue:123) and src/App.vue:1492 handles it with `@contextmenu="() => {}"`.
findings.repro: 1. Open the working copy tab. 2. Click the checkbox at the left of any file row: nothing is checked and nothing changes. 3. Right-click a row: no context menu appears. (Both controls are visible affordances on every row.)
findings.expected: Either the checkbox works (multi-select → bulk stage/discard) or it is not rendered; the right-click menu offers the per-row verbs.
findings.actual: Every file row shows a checkbox that cannot be checked, and right-clicking a row does nothing.
findings.fix: Either pass a `selectedPaths` model and forward `@toggle` (and use it for bulk verbs), or remove the checkbox and the `@contextmenu.prevent` binding until multi-select exists.
findings.testIdea: Mounted WorkingCopyPane test: assert `.file-check` is absent when no selection model is supplied, and that clicking it emits `toggle` to the parent when one is supplied.

crossCutting: The only guard against dead controls is structurally blind to exactly this failure mode. /tmp/meridian-baseline/src/interactionCompleteness.test.ts proves that 'every emitted event is listened for' by regexing event NAMES across all sources and asserting each name appears somewhere — so binding `@contextmenu="() => {}"` in App.vue satisfies it. Fifteen such bindings exist in App.vue alone (lines 1424, 1492, 1560, 1568, 1593, 1655, 1663, 1679-1682, 1686-1687, 1705, 1747). Every one of them renders a translated, enabled, screen-reader-announced control. Fix once, not per finding: make the check reject empty arrow bodies (and no-op identifiers), or delete the controls.

One `LoadState` type serves two different jobs — 'what should I render' and 'did the last action work' — and each store picks its own failure convention. branches turns throws into `null`/`false` plus a shared `lastError` (stores/branches.ts:46-95); history nulls the graph and swallows (stores/history.ts:79-84); repos empties `remotes` on failure (stores/repos.ts:49-51); workingCopy lets a mutation error replace the entire tab. The result is that 'failed' and 'there is none' are pixel-identical in every surface, and the message the user sees depends on which store the verb happened to go through. Fix once: one result type carrying the `ErrorPayload`, one reporting path, and mutation errors that never overwrite list state.

There is no in-flight guard and no cancellation anywhere in the app. `useGit.busy` is set and read by nobody; the only guard in the codebase is the `inFlight` promise in useApp.ts; the Rust queue serialises per repository but the UI neither shows nor blocks queued work. Every verb is double-clickable, fetch/push/clone/install cannot be abandoned, and every async store load (history query, branch list, remotes) is last-response-wins with no generation counter, so a slow earlier response can overwrite a faster later one. Fix once: a per-repo operation registry (start / settle / cancel + request token) that every verb goes through and that simultaneously drives the disabled state and the activity chip.

Selection and query state is duplicated between shell refs and the stores that own the data, and the copies silently drift. `branchSearch`/`branchFilter` (App.vue:1086-1087) never reach `useBranches.search`, so the engine-side `search` argument of `branch_list` is always empty; `historySearch`/`historyView` are shell refs that re-drive the store through an undebounced watcher (App.vue:1075); `selectedBranchName`, `selectedSidebarId`, `paletteQuery` are all shell-local. Fix once: one owner per piece of state, in the store, with the shell holding only view state that has no server meaning.

Limits and capacities are decided ad hoc per surface and mostly fail silently: diffs truncate at 40k lines, history pages at 250, branches load everything and filter locally, the activity list caps at 50, remotes load all. Each surface decides on its own whether truncation is visible, which is why the working-copy findings about silent diff truncation and about rows that can never appear are two instances of one missing contract. Fix once: a `Paginated`/`Truncated` field on `LoadState` that every load must state, rendered by one component.

Error presentation is decided at the call site, not at a boundary: raw engine English, a shell toast, or a ListShell error arm, chosen per verb; the i18n `errors.byCode` catalogue is bypassed. `useAppEvents` is the only place with a systematic rule (ignore events for another repo) and it does not extend to the stores' own awaits. Fix once: a single error-to-catalogue mapping at the reporting boundary, plus the repo-id check on every async store result.

Nothing re-reads state that changed outside the app's own commands. Refreshes come only from `refsChanged`/`workingCopyChanged` events and the explicit ⌘⇧R / palette refresh — no window-focus refresh, no file watcher — and even the manual refresh skips `compare` and the remotes list. An edit made in a terminal leaves the entire window stale until the user remembers the shortcut.

All state is global singleton state: one `repos.selectedId`, one history selection, one branch selection, one toast list, one dialogue queue, one activity list — with no per-window isolation and no request tagging. Every cross-repo correctness question in the findings (a status delta from the previous repo, an event arriving after a switch, a queue entry outliving its operation) is an instance of this one structural choice.
